subject: history_social
notes: Skara Brae is a village on the Orkney Islands, off the north coast of Scotland, that was inhabited from about 3100 to 2500 BCE.
It was uncovered in 1850 when a storm stripped away the sand and grass that had buried it.
Each house contains beds, shelves, and a central hearth, all built from flat slabs of local stone.
Orkney had almost no trees, so wood for building was scarce.
Because the stone furniture survived, the houses are among the best-preserved Neolithic homes in Europe.
stem: The student wants to explain why the furniture at Skara Brae was made of stone. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Each house at Skara Brae contains beds, shelves, and a central hearth, all built from flat slabs of local stone.
choices.B: Because its stone furniture survived, Skara Brae is among the best-preserved Neolithic villages in Europe.
choices.C: Skara Brae was uncovered in 1850 when a storm stripped away the sand and grass that had buried it for thousands of years.
choices.D: The people of Skara Brae built their beds and shelves from flat slabs of stone because Orkney had almost no trees, so wood for building was scarce.

explanation.why: The goal asks for a cause. The fourth note supplies it: there was almost no wood on Orkney. The key must connect the stone furniture to that shortage of wood.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This describes the stone furniture but gives no reason for it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This uses "because," but it explains a result of the stone furniture, the good preservation, not the reason the furniture was stone.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This tells how the village was found, not why its furniture is stone.
explanation.D: Correct. "Because" links the stone furniture to the lack of trees, the reason given in the notes.
